newsitem.title: USA: White House urges Senate move on Lake nomination.
newsitem.headline: White House urges Senate move on Lake nomination.

text.p: The White House Tuesday signaled frustration at delays in Senate confirmation of Anthony Lake as CIA director, saying President Clinton needs an intelligence chief.

"The president has a very ambitious and active foreign policy schedule in the coming weeks and months, one in which we will need a strong and effective director of Central Intelligence that can help prepare the information and analysis that's necessary for good policy-making," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

"Tony Lake is a superb nominee to bring that kind of wisdom to the president's foreign policy-making team. And for that the president has urged publicly and privately that the Senate move to expeditious consideration," he said.

McCurry's comments came after the chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, Sen. Richard Shelby, R-Ala., postponed Lake's confirmation hearings for the second time, this time until March 11, to look into "many unanswered questions" about Lake's stock dealings and disputed congressional testimony.
McCurry said the White House felt Lake had answered the questions about him and in any case was in a good position to clarify any concerns without delaying his hearings until March.

"But we will have to live with the schedule that is determined by the Senate given their constitutional role. We would just point out that we have an ample need to have strong leadership within the intelligence community as we move into the weeks ahead," McCurry said. Clinton has a number of foreign trips coming up in the next several months, including a March summit with Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
